fields.options:
Add this to your Print Format's HTML. Leave Anchor Text above at its default - the same value works for every template regardless of size, since size lives entirely in the HTML, not here:

<div style="width:160px; height:40px; color:#ffffff; overflow:hidden;">##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR:160x40##</div>

A plain block-level div with explicit width/height - no position:absolute, no inline-block - reliably reserves that much space in the page's normal layout flow, and the anchor text sits at its top-left by default with no extra positioning needed. (An earlier version of this guidance used position:absolute, which some PDF engines don't reliably reserve space for - if a stamp has overlapped or drifted below where it should be, switch to this plain div instead.)

The :WxH suffix is optional and detected automatically from what's actually rendered - add it in the Print Format's HTML to size that particular template; leaving it off (plain ##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR##) falls back to 160x80. There's no hidden default forcing a taller box - if 80 (or 40, or whatever) is too tall or too short for how many stamp fields you have enabled in Settings, just change the number.

Keep the div's own width/height matching the number in the anchor text exactly - the div reserves the layout space, and the anchor text tells the signing code how big to actually draw the stamp; if the two disagree, the stamp will be sized correctly but may not fit the space reserved for it.

The stamp is drawn extending downward-right from exactly where the anchor text sits (its top-left), filling the box below/right of it. The stamp content is centered (both directions) within that box automatically.

Use color:#ffffff (matching the background), not opacity:0 - some PDF engines skip painting opacity:0 text entirely, dropping it from the searchable text layer too. If the surrounding background isn't white, match this color to it instead.
